source_caption:
Joe Pantoliano wasn’t the first choice to play Ralph Cifaretto in The Sopranos.

Ray Liotta was reportedly approached for the role but turned it down, partly because he didn’t want to return to familiar mob territory after Goodfellas. Even more surprisingly, Robert Funaro was originally cast as Ralph and had already started working on the show. Creator David Chase eventually decided he wasn’t right for the part, but kept Funaro around and later cast him as Eugene Pontecorvo.That opened the door for Pantoliano.

Pantoliano initially had doubts about returning to television, but Chase convinced him to take the role. The actor then developed his own backstory for Ralph and helped shape his distinctive appearance, including the expensive suits and ascots that separated him from Tony’s other associates.

Ralph joined the series in Season 3 and quickly became one of its most unpredictable characters. Pantoliano managed to make him funny, charismatic and deeply disturbing at the same time. The performance eventually earned Pantoliano the 2003 Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series proving the casting change worked out pretty well.

source_details.synopsis: The Sopranos is an American crime drama television series created by David Chase for HBO. The series follows Tony Soprano (James Gandolfini), a New Jersey Mafia boss. Suffering from panic attacks, he reluctantly begins seeing psychiatrist Dr. Jennifer Melfi (Lorraine Bracco), who encourages him to open up about his difficulties balancing his family life with his criminal activities. Other important characters include Tony's family, Mafia colleagues, and rivals, most notably his wife Carmela (Edie Falco), his nephew and protégé Christopher Moltisanti (Michael Imperioli), and his uncle Corrado "Junior" Soprano (Dominic Chianese). Greenlit in 1997, the series was broadcast on HBO from January 1
